evaluators.suitabilityLead: The 5 canonical criteria (handbook 3.2) — a good GenAI candidate meets these.

criteria.c1: The activity is language/text-based or knowledge work
criteria.c3: Errors are tolerable or the output is cheap to verify
criteria.c4: The input data is available and legally usable
criteria.c5: Regulatory risk is low initially (back-office first, customer-facing later)

evaluators.readinessLead: 4 dimensions, 3 grades — the weakest dimension dominates (weakest-link rule).
evaluators.aiActLead: Guided questions produce a SUGGESTION — you confirm the classification.

questions.annex3: Does it touch an Annex III area (e.g. creditworthiness, HR recruitment/evaluation, access to essential services)?
questions.interacts: Does the system interact directly with people, or generate outbound AI content?
questions.prohibited: Does it involve a prohibited practice (social scoring, manipulative techniques, emotion recognition at work/in education)?

evaluators.warnNotice: Prohibited or high-risk suggestion — a note is required. There is no automatic exclusion: the decision is yours.
evaluators.omnibusInfo: Info: high-risk obligations apply from 2027-12-02 under the Digital Omnibus.

manage_closely.title: Manage closely — resolve concerns early.
manage_closely.body: High influence and high exposure: their support is essential to the decision. Engage early, share plans, and address concerns before they escalate.

keep_satisfied.title: Keep satisfied — don't overload with detail.
keep_satisfied.body: High influence, lower exposure: you need their sign-off but not their attention to daily detail. Keep it concise and decision-focused; get explicit approval at key points.

keep_informed.title: Keep informed — the day-to-day impact lands here.
keep_informed.body: Lower influence, high exposure: the change affects them directly. Update regularly and gather feedback; their buy-in helps adoption.

monitor.title: Monitor — low priority for now.
monitor.body: Low influence and low exposure: minimal, periodic updates are enough. Watch for their role changing as the project progresses.

p2.title: Benefit calculation
p2.stage1Hint: — what you enter, or the AI suggests from a concrete source
p2.stage2Tag: DECISION POINT · HUMAN ONLY · AI NEVER FILLS
p2.fekHint: How much of the freed capacity actually becomes a cost saving.
p2.lockedHint: The derived values cannot be computed until the brake is set.
p2.emptyLead: The benefit is a derived chain. Start with the inputs — the AI suggests a value if the raw material gives a concrete basis.
p2.suggestOnlyInputs: The AI suggests the inputs — never the brake.
p2.benefitConfirmedNote: Inputs confirmed · the brake is a human decision
p2.ruleHint: — what we do after the measurement
p2.scalePlaceholder: if threshold met → what we do
p2.pivotPlaceholder: if half met → what we do
p2.stopPlaceholder: if not met → what we do
p2.pokaYokeBody: The pilot cannot start until the success threshold and all three decision branches (scale / pivot / stop) are filled. This is the phase's poka-yoke: success is decided up front, not after the fact.
p2.filledConfirm: Success pre-recorded — the pilot can start.
p2.e1Prerecorded: Success defined up front — not after the fact, by feel
p2.scaleThenPlaceholder: e.g. to the full B2C queue

processMap.errInputNotFound: The selected input was not found in the project.
processMap.noticeNoSteps: Processing finished but produced no identifiable process step — check the source.
processMap.errAsIsNotFound: The AS-IS process map was not found — generate it first.
processMap.errMapNotFound: The process map was not found.
processMap.errChatApproved: An approved map can no longer be edited from chat — start a new iteration.
processMap.errChatEmpty: Describe what the assistant should change.
processMap.errChatNoPending: No pending proposal on this message — ask for a new one in chat.
processMap.chatNoChangeReply: I did not prepare a change for this request — clarify which step to modify.
processMap.chatAppliedMsg: Applied: {added} new, {modified} modified, {removed} removed step(s). Marked on the diagram — review before approval; the original AI version is preserved.
processMap.chatSubtitle: edits the structured step list — never the source

processMap.chatThinking: The assistant is preparing a proposal…
processMap.chatHitlNote: The assistant proposes — you apply the change and you approve the process (HITL).
processMap.indexLead: The client process in two states: AS-IS (how it works today) and TO-BE (how it will with the AI solution). The AI builds a walkable process map from the raw transcript — you correct it, then approve it as a whole. The raw source is never overwritten.
processMap.asisColLead: The current process extracted from the raw transcript — every step with a source reference.
processMap.tobeColLead: The future process — with AI entry points and mandatory human control (HITL).
processMap.noInputs: No raw material — add a transcript in the phase workspace Input zone first.
processMap.tobeAiNeedsAsis: The AS-IS map is needed first — the AI designs from it and the pain points.
processMap.errPickInput: Pick a transcript to generate from.
processMap.summaryAsis: AS-IS · {steps} steps · {open} open points — every step extracted from the raw transcript, traceable back to it.
processMap.summaryTobe: TO-BE · under editing — the AI enters at {ai} points, with {hitl} mandatory human controls (HITL). {steps} steps.
processMap.summaryTobeApproved: TO-BE · approved (v{v}) · the AI enters at {ai} points with {hitl} HITL controls. The original AI version is preserved.
processMap.summaryCmp: What changes: AS-IS {a} steps → TO-BE {b} steps — switch back to a mode for details.
processMap.approvedNote: the approved version is locked · the original AI version is preserved · work continues in a new iteration
processMap.iterateFreely: iterate freely — approve as a whole at the end
processMap.emptyAsis: No AS-IS process map for this view yet.
processMap.emptyTobe: No TO-BE process map for this view yet.
processMap.hintOverview: Click a step to start walking · the canvas is draggable
processMap.hintFocus: Pick a branch in the panel · drag the canvas · ⤢ full map
processMap.hintCmp: AS-IS left · TO-BE right — switch back to a mode for details
processMap.sourceHighlighted: highlighted: the passage tied to the current step · {loc}
processMap.ovTitleAsis: The whole AS-IS process on one map
processMap.ovTitleTobe: The whole TO-BE process on one map
processMap.ovDescAsis: Green pill for start/end, blue diamond for decisions, grey card for human steps, blue for system steps. Every step was extracted from the raw transcript and can be traced back to it.
processMap.ovDescTobe: Purple cards are AI entry points, amber is mandatory human control (HITL). A dashed border marks a step inserted via chat editing.
processMap.ovHint: Click a step to start walking — at decisions you pick a branch here.
processMap.endNote: End state. “↶ Last decision” for the other branch, or “⤢ Full map”.
processMap.diffNoteNewDefault: New step — added from the conversation; it was not in the original AI version. Compare with the “Show original” toggle.
processMap.diffNoteModDefault: This step changed compared to the original AI version. Compare with the “Show original” toggle.
processMap.noSourceRef: This step has no source reference.
processMap.dataModelSoon: The backend data-model binding is not live yet. The tables and fields this step reads / writes will appear here.
processMap.noOpenPoints: No open question for this step.
processMap.noCrumbs: — start walking by clicking a node
processMap.cmpMissing: Comparison needs both AS-IS and TO-BE — generate the missing one on the entry page.
processMap.expectedImpactNone: No metric binding — the expected impact will come from the business case thresholds; we do not estimate a number here.
processMap.cmpFooter: Click the AS-IS or TO-BE toggle for the detailed walk.
processMap.legendNote: The type set is not fixed — it adapts to the process (business / technical) and is extensible.

requirements.title: Requirements & stories
requirements.agileLockedHint: Stories are derived from system requirements — build the tree first.
requirements.lineageHint: Click a card — its lineage and bound stories light up.
requirements.agileNote: Stories are derived from system requirements — every story lists its covered requirement chip(s). The direction is fixed: requirement → story.
requirements.emptyBizText: Everything below decomposes from here — and stories derive from it too.
requirements.emptyShNote: A business requirement is needed first.
requirements.emptySysNote: System requirements attach to a stakeholder need.
requirements.aiTreeNote: Or let the AI propose a starting tree from the TO-BE process and the pain points — you edit and confirm it, then derive the stories from it.
requirements.agileEmptyText: No user stories yet. Stories are derived from the confirmed system requirements — the AI proposes an epic-packaged set, you confirm each.
requirements.genStoriesNote: E1: the proposal is ai_suggested — confirm or reject per card.
requirements.uncoveredCta: {id} is not covered yet — derive a story
requirements.moscowUnsetHint: MoSCoW not set — human judgement decides.
requirements.panelNoParent: No parent candidates on this level yet — add the upper level first.
requirements.panelTextPlaceholder: E.g. The system logs every proposal approval/edit for audit purposes.
requirements.panelAddNote: After saving, add GWT ACs and derive stories.
requirements.panelCoveredNote: Multiple requirements can be bound — this is the N:M link.
requirements.panelAiNote: The AI drafts a proposal from the covered requirements — the shared AC is inherited automatically. You finalize it.
requirements.panelDeriveNote: The shared AC comes from the requirement — the story does not copy it.
requirements.acHitlNote: The AI drafts — you edit and save (HITL).
requirements.acSharedFormNote: The AC lives on the requirement — bound stories show it automatically.
requirements.bidirectionalNote: The link is bidirectional — this requirement shows on the story too.
requirements.nmNote: {id} is also covered by another story — this is the many-to-many link.
requirements.acSharedNote: The same AC as on the covered requirement — not a duplicate. Editing updates both places.
requirements.sharedAcBridge: Not a copy — the same object. Edit the AC on the requirement and the story updates instantly. This is the bridge between the formal requirement and the delivery story; traceability is bidirectional.
requirements.errAlreadyHasTree: A requirement tree already exists — the AI proposal only runs into an empty tree.
requirements.errAlreadyHasStories: Stories already exist — the derivation proposal only runs on an empty set.
requirements.errNoSystemReqs: No system requirements — stories can only derive from them.
requirements.noticeNoBasis: The run completed but produced no proposal — check the source material.
requirements.errParentRequired: The parent (tree link) is required on this level.
requirements.errAcMissing: All three of GIVEN / WHEN / THEN are required.
requirements.errCoverRequired: At least one covered requirement is required — the direction is fixed: requirement → story.
requirements.errCoverSystemOnly: A story may only cover SYSTEM-level requirements.
requirements.noticeNoAc: Generation produced no AC derivable from the text — refine the requirement wording, or add one manually.
